quotes.text: Companies aren't afraid of copilot agents themselves. They're afraid of losing sight of them. They're afraid of forgetting who built which agent, when it was last reviewed, or why it's pulling information from sensitive systems.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes AI hesitation as a visibility problem rather than a technology problem.

quotes.text: A better model is to allow broader participation in building ideas while limiting deployment authority to designated roles.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete, reusable governance principle that separates building from publishing.

quotes.text: Permissions and policies are like fences. They tell employees where they are allowed to build and what tools they can use. But without visibility, you have no way of knowing whether someone wandered into an unchecked corner
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains clearly why monitoring must complement permissions.

quotes.text: A common pattern is that admins assume activation equals governance. A new feature shows up in the admin center, the switch is flipped on, and everyone feels like the job is done.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names a common governance mistake in a memorable way.

quotes.text: Governance isn't about slowing down teams. It's about making sure their efforts last beyond the first exciting prototype.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Positions governance as an enabler of lasting innovation.

takeaways: The guardrails for Copilot agents already live in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center, where admins can see which agents exist, what connectors they use and who can publish them.
Copilot Studio lets employees experiment safely when admins restrict connectors, actions and publishing rights to designated roles.
Permissions alone are not governance: audit logs, usage monitoring and consistent policies aligned with security and compliance teams are what keep agents under control.
hook: AI agents rarely fail loudly; they multiply quietly without owners, version history or audit trails. This episode is for Microsoft 365 admins and IT governance teams who want to enable Copilot agents without losing oversight. You will learn how the Admin Center, Copilot Studio controls and monitoring work together as a practical governance framework.
